### **Project Overview**

This is a tech portfolio website designed to showcase my work and accomplishments as well as to serve as an introduction to potential employers and collaborators. It was designed entirely using HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

### **Target audience**

The target audience is primarily for employers and hiring managers while I welcome potential collaborators as well.

### **Content strategy**

The site was designed to be clean and professional. To enforce the clean strategy the site encloses sections within flexboxes and several cards to keep things neat.

### **Information organization**

 The site contains a prominent hero section followed by about me, skills, projects and education, and contact sections.

### **Interaction / functionality**

The navbar header allows scrolling to various sections and a hover effect was utilized with cards as well as a change of color on hover effect.

### **Technical overview**

This site was designed entirely using HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

### **Timeline / project milestone**

Development began in February 2026 and went live on March 12th, 2026\.

### **PART 2: DESIGN**

1. **What overall style will best represent you?** **Clean, professional, and minimalist** to reflect a structured, detail-oriented engineering mindset.  
2. **What color scheme will you use and why?** Professional blues paired with crisp whites and light grays. Blue conveys trust, logic, and technology, while white ensures a clean, readable aesthetic.  
3. **What fonts will you use for headings and body text?** Modern, readable sans-serif fonts like **Quicksand** or **Open Sans** for a tech-focused look.  
4. **How will your design reflect your personality or field?** The highly organized and logical layout will reflect both my analytical chemistry background and precise coding practices.  
5. **What layout will your homepage follow?** A clear header with my tagline, a brief intro, followed by a skills section and a section highlighting my top 3 technical projects.  
6. **How will you organize project sections visually?** Using a **card-based flex layout**, where each card features a project title and a brief description.  
7. **Will the site be mobile-friendly? How will you ensure responsiveness?** Yes, by utilizing responsive CSS techniques like **Flexbox or CSS Grid**.  
8. **What visual hierarchy will guide visitors?** Large, bold headings for main sections and prominent project visuals to draw the eye directly to my work.  
9. **How will consistency be maintained across pages?** The site will be a single page  
10. **How will accessibility be considered?** By using readable font sizes, adding meaningful HTML tags, and including `alt` text for all images.  
11. **Will you use icons, images, or illustrations? Why?** Yes, I will use **tech stack icons** (like the Python or Git logos) for quick visual scanning, and **actual screenshots or diagrams** of my projects instead of generic stock photos.  
12. **What portfolio websites inspired your design?** Professional software developer portfolios that focus heavily on clean code presentation and problem-solving case studies.

### **PART 3: INTERACTIVITY**

1. **What interactive elements will your site include?** A sticky navigation menu and hover effects on project cards and links.  
2. **Will your site include a contact form? How will it work?** No, there will be an email and GitHub link on the site.  
3. **What JavaScript features will you implement?** Javascript will be used to ensure proper scrolling functionality.  
4. **How will users receive feedback from interactions?** Cards will change color or slightly elevate when hovered over.  
5. **How does interactivity improve the user experience?** It makes the site feel modern, responsive, and engaging, while actively demonstrating my frontend development and JavaScript skills to potential employers.
